description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simple Kalman filter for sensor fusion. The module should take in two sensor measurements (sensor1 and sensor2), and an estimated position as input. It should output a refined estimated position based on the Kalman filter equations. Assume fixed parameters for the Kalman filter such as process noise covariance and measurement noise covariance. Handle both the prediction and update steps of the Kalman filter in a clocked process.
code:
module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input signed [15:0] sensor1,
    input signed [15:0] sensor2,
    input signed [15:0] estimated_position,
    output reg signed [15:0] refined_position
);
    // Kalman filter parameters (for simplicity)
    parameter signed [15:0] Q = 16'h0001; // Process noise covariance
    parameter signed [15:0] R = 16'h0004; // Measurement noise covariance
    reg signed [15:0] P; // Estimation error covariance
    reg signed [15:0] K; // Kalman gain
    reg signed [15:0] z; // Measurement
    reg signed [15:0] x; // Updated estimate

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            refined_position <= 16'h0000;
            P <= 16'h0001; // Initial guess for P
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            P <= P + Q;

            // Measurement update step
            z <= (sensor1 + sensor2) >> 1; // Average of sensors
            K <= P / (P + R); // Kalman gain
            x <= estimated_position + K * (z - estimated_position); // Update the estimate
            P <= (16'h0001 - K) * P; // Update the error covariance

            refined_position <= x; // Output the refined position
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a PCIe endpoint controller state machine that responds to a request signal. The state machine should have the following states: IDLE, REQUEST_RECEIVED, DATA_TRANSFER, and COMPLETED. The state machine should transition from IDLE to REQUEST_RECEIVED on a request signal, then to DATA_TRANSFER when data is ready, and finally to COMPLETED when the transfer is done. The state machine should reset back to IDLE on a reset signal.
code:
module pcie_endpoint_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input request,
    input data_ready,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00 - IDLE, 01 - REQUEST_RECEIVED, 10 - DATA_TRANSFER, 11 - COMPLETED
);

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, 
              REQUEST_RECEIVED = 2'b01,
              DATA_TRANSFER = 2'b10,
              COMPLETED = 2'b11;

    // Sequential logic for state transitions
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (request) begin
                        state <= REQUEST_RECEIVED;
                    end
                end
                REQUEST_RECEIVED: begin
                    if (data_ready) begin
                        state <= DATA_TRANSFER;
                    end
                end
                DATA_TRANSFER: begin
                    state <= COMPLETED;
                end
                COMPLETED: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE after completing
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

        end else if (enable) begin

description: Design a 16-bit serializer that takes a 16-bit parallel input and outputs the bits serially. The serializer should have a clock signal that shifts out one bit at each clock cycle. The design should include an enable signal that controls when the serialization should occur. When the enable signal is low, the output should remain in a high-impedance state. The output should be a single output line that represents the serialized data.
code:
module serializer(
    input wire clk,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [15:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [3:0] bit_count; // 4 bits to count 16 shifts

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (enable) begin
            if (bit_count < 16) begin
                serial_out <= parallel_in[15 - bit_count]; // Shift out MSB first
                bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
            end else begin
                serial_out <= 1'bz; // High impedance state
            end
        end else begin
            serial_out <= 1'bz; // High impedance when not enabled
            bit_count <= 0; // Reset count when not enabled
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit serializer that takes an 8-bit parallel input and serializes it into a single output bitstream. The serialization occurs on the rising edge of a clock signal, and the output should be valid for a specific number of clock cycles (in this case, 8 cycles). After the 8 bits have been serialized, the output should remain low until the next serialization process is initiated. The circuit should have a reset signal to initialize the state.
code:
module serializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire start,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count; // Counter for the bits being serialized
    reg [7:0] shift_reg; // Shift register for the input data

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            serial_out <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 0;
        end else if (start) begin
            shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
            bit_count <= 7;        // Set counter to the last bit index
        end else if (bit_count != 0) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[bit_count]; // Output the current bit
            bit_count <= bit_count - 1;         // Decrement the counter
        end else begin
            serial_out <= 0; // Output low when no bits are left to send
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that performs 3x3 image convolution operation. The module should take a 3x3 matrix as input and a 3-bit binary number as a kernel. The output should be a single 8-bit value representing the convolution result. Assume the input matrix values and kernel values are provided as 8-bit unsigned integers. The kernel should be represented as a 9-bit value, where the MSB is the scaling factor for the output. Implement the logic to multiply corresponding elements and sum them to produce the output.
code:

    input [71:0] matrix, // 3x3 matrix, 8 bits each (total 72 bits)
    input [8:0] kernel,  // 3-bit binary kernel with scaling factor
    output reg [7:0] result // 8-bit output
);

    end
endmodule

description: Design a Watchdog Timer in Verilog that resets a system if it does not receive a reset signal within a specified timeout period. The timer should generate a timeout signal if the reset signal is not received for a given number of clock cycles.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst, // Active high reset signal
    output reg timeout // Timeout signal
);
    parameter TIMEOUT_CYCLES = 8; // Number of clock cycles before timeout
    reg [3:0] counter; // 4-bit counter to keep track of clock cycles

    // Sequential logic
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            counter <= 0;
            timeout <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (counter < TIMEOUT_CYCLES - 1) begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
                timeout <= 0; // Not timed out yet
            end else begin
                timeout <= 1; // Timed out
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

The serializer should have an enable signal that controls when the serialization occurs. Additionally, the serializer should reset its output and internal state when a reset signal is asserted.

    input rst_n,

            bit_index <= 0;

description:

where input_value is the 8-bit input and V_ref is 5V. Implement the DAC such that it produces the correct analog voltage level for the provided 8-bit input values.

Design a Fractional-N PLL (Phase-Locked Loop) in Verilog that adjusts the output frequency based on a fractional divider. The PLL should have an input clock, a reset signal, and a control signal to set the fractional value for frequency division. The output of the PLL should be a clock that reflects the desired frequency.
code:
module fractional_n_pll (
    input wire clk_in,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] fractional_value, // 8-bit fractional value for division
    output reg clk_out
);
    
    reg [7:0] counter;
    reg [15:0] divisor; // to hold the full division value including fractional part
    
    always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            clk_out <= 0;
            divisor <= 256; // default divisor
        end else begin
            if (counter < divisor) begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
            end else begin
                counter <= 0;
                clk_out <= ~clk_out; // toggle output clock
            end
        end
    end
    
    always @(fractional_value) begin
        divisor <= 256 + fractional_value; // adjust divisor based on fractional value
    end
    
endmodule

module dram_cell (

    input wire WE,        // Write enable
    input wire BL,        // Bit line
    input wire reset,     // Reset signal
    output reg Q          // Stored data
);

        if (reset) begin

endmodule

description: Design a watchdog timer that resets an output signal if no input signal is received for a specified timeout period. The timer should allow for a configurable timeout duration and should reset the output signal if the timer expires before the input signal is received again. The input signal is a single-bit signal that indicates an active state, and the output signal is also a single-bit signal that indicates whether the watchdog timer is active (1) or has timed out (0).
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire input_signal,
    input wire [3:0] timeout_duration, // timeout duration in clock cycles
    output reg output_signal
);
    reg [3:0] counter;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            output_signal <= 1; // Active state
        end else begin
            if (input_signal) begin
                counter <= 0; // Reset counter on input signal
                output_signal <= 1; // Watchdog is active
            end else begin
                if (counter < timeout_duration) begin
                    counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
                end else begin
                    output_signal <= 0; // Watchdog timeout
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a 4-bit down counter with an asynchronous reset. The counter should count down from a predefined value (e.g., 15) to 0. When it reaches 0, it should wrap around back to 15 on the next clock cycle. The counter should reset to 15 when the reset signal is activated.

description: Design a Hamming (7,4) encoder. The encoder should take 4 data bits as input and produce a 7-bit encoded output that includes the parity bits for error correction purposes. The parity bits should be calculated based on the input data bits according to the Hamming code rules.

module hamming_encoder (
    input [3:0] data,
    output [6:0] code
);

assign p3 = data[1] ^ data[2] ^ data[3]; // parity bit P3

assign code[5] = p2; // code bit 5
assign code[4] = data[0]; // code bit 4
assign code[3] = p3; // code bit 3

module bluetooth_signal_controller (

    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    output reg signal_out
);

        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            signal_out <= 0;
        end else if (start) begin

            signal_out <= 0; // Reset the output
        end else if (counter > 0 && counter < DELAY_CYCLES) begin
            counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
        end else if (counter == DELAY_CYCLES) begin

    end

The serial data should be valid on the rising edge of the clock. Use a 3-bit counter to keep track of the number of bits received. Once 8 bits are received, the output should be available for one clock cycle before being updated with the next set of incoming bits.

    input wire serial_in,
    output reg [7:0] parallel_out,
    output reg data_valid
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

        if (bit_count < 8) begin
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], serial_in}; // Shift in the new bit
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
            data_valid <= 0; // Data not valid until 8 bits are received
        end
        if (bit_count == 7) begin
            data_valid <= 1; // Data is valid when 8 bits are received
            parallel_out <= shift_reg; // Output the 8 bits
        end

    end
endmodule

If an ERROR condition is detected (for simplicity, we can use a signal `error` that goes high), it transitions to the ERROR state. The state machine should also provide the current state as output.
code:
module sata_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input error,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: ACTIVE, 10: ERROR
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // IDLE
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // IDLE
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // ACTIVE
                    end
                end
                2'b01: begin // ACTIVE
                    if (error) begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // ERROR
                    end else if (!start) begin
                        state <= 2'b00; // IDLE
                    end
                end
                2'b10: begin // ERROR
                    if (reset) begin
                        state <= 2'b00; // IDLE
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

- It should have a parallel load input, a clock input, and a reset input.
- On the rising edge of the clock, if the load signal is high, the data should be loaded into the register.
- If the load signal is low, the data should shift out of the register one bit at a time.
- The output should reflect the current state of the register.
code:
module PIPO_Shift_Register #(parameter N = 8) (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire load,
    input wire [N-1:0] data_in,
    output reg [N-1:0] data_out
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            data_out <= 0; // Clear register on reset
        end else if (load) begin
            data_out <= data_in; // Load data in parallel
        end else begin
            data_out <= {data_out[N-2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a fixed-priority arbiter in Verilog. When a request is granted, it should remain granted until the corresponding request signal is deactivated. The arbiter should handle one grant at a time according to the priority of the request signals.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            grant <= 4'b0000; // Reset all grants to 0
        end else begin
            case (req)
                4'b0001: grant <= 4'b0001; // Grant req[0]
                4'b0010: grant <= (grant == 4'b0000) ? 4'b0010 : grant; // Grant req[1] if no higher priority
                4'b0100: grant <= (grant == 4'b0000) ? 4'b0100 : grant; // Grant req[2] if no higher priority
                4'b1000: grant <= (grant == 4'b0000) ? 4'b1000 : grant; // Grant req[3] if no higher priority
                default: grant <= 4'b0000; // No grant if no requests
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

module branch_predictor(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [1:0] address,
    input branch_taken,
    output reg prediction
);
    reg [1:0] state [0:3]; // 4 entries for 2-bit states
    integer i;

    initial begin
        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            state[i] = 2'b00; // Initialize all states to 00
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                state[i] <= 2'b00; // Reset all states to 00
            end
        end else begin
            prediction <= (state[address] == 2'b10 || state[address] == 2'b11); // Predict Taken

            case (state[address])
                2'b00: if (branch_taken) state[address] <= 2'b01; else state[address] <= 2'b00;
                2'b01: if (branch_taken) state[address] <= 2'b10; else state[address] <= 2'b00;
                2'b10: if (branch_taken) state[address] <= 2'b11; else state[address] <= 2'b01;

        end
    end
endmodule

);

5. The output should be the transmitted data and the state of the system.

The states of the FSM should be:
- IDLE: waiting for data to be sent
- SENDING: sending data
- WAIT_ACK: waiting for ACK

module ARQ_System (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [4:0] data_in,
    input wire ack,
    output reg [4:0] data_out,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: SENDING, 10: WAIT_ACK, 11: ERROR
);

    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE = 2'b00, 
               SENDING = 2'b01, 
               WAIT_ACK = 2'b10, 
               ERROR = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            attempt <= 2'b00;
            data_out <= 5'b00000;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Load data to send
                    state <= SENDING; // Move to sending state
                    attempt <= 2'b00; // Reset attempts
                end
                SENDING: begin
                    state <= WAIT_ACK; // Move to wait for ACK

                WAIT_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // ACK received, go back to IDLE
                    end else begin
                        attempt <= attempt + 1; // Increment attempt
                        if (attempt >= 2'b10) begin
                            state <= ERROR; // Maximum attempts reached
                        end else begin
                            state <= SENDING; // Resend data
                        end
                    end
                end
                ERROR: begin
                    // Handle error state (can be expanded for logging, etc.)
                    data_out <= 5'b11111; // Indicate error in output
                end
                default: state <= IDLE; // Default to IDLE
            endcase
        end

    reg [7:0] shift_reg;
    reg [2:0] bit_count;

               START = 4'd1,
               SEND = 4'd2,
               STOP = 4'd3;

        if (enable) begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    SDA <= 1; // Idle state of SDA
                    SCL <= 1; // Idle state of SCL
                    state <= START;

                    SCL <= 1;
                    state <= SEND;
                    shift_reg <= data; // Load data to shift register
                    bit_count <= 7; // Prepare to send 8 bits

                SEND: begin

                    SCL <= 1; // Clock high
                    if (bit_count == 0)

                    else

                end
                STOP: begin
                    SDA <= 0; // Prepare for stop condition

                    SDA <= 1; // Stop condition

            endcase

    output reg [8:0] img_out  // 3x3 binary output image (flattened)  
);

            if (img_in[i]) begin

                if (i % 3 > 0) img_out[i - 1] = 1;      // left

                if (i / 3 > 0) img_out[i - 3] = 1;      // top

    input signed [15:0] x,      // input sample
    output reg signed [15:0] y   // output sample

    parameter signed [15:0] b0 = 16'h0A00; // coefficient for x[n]
    parameter signed [15:0] b1 = 16'h0A00; // coefficient for x[n-1]
    parameter signed [15:0] b2 = 16'h0A00; // coefficient for x[n-2]
    parameter signed [15:0] a1 = 16'hF000; // coefficient for y[n-1]
    parameter signed [15:0] a2 = 16'hF000; // coefficient for y[n-2]

        if (rst) begin
            z1 <= 16'h0000;
            z2 <= 16'h0000;
            y <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin
            y <= (b0 * x + b1 * z1 + b2 * z2 - a1 * y - a2 * (y - z1)) >>> 15; // Fixed-point multiplication and shifting
